newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.S. office in Pakistan evacuated due to bomb hoax.
newsitem.headline: U.S. office in Pakistan evacuated due to bomb hoax.

text.p: The United States Information Service (USIS) centre in Islamabad was evacuated on Thursday after receiving a bomb threat that police said later was a hoax.
A USIS official said an unidentified caller had said a bomb had been placed in the American Centre building. The building was evacuated while police searched the premises.
"However, no bomb was found and the call proved a hoax," said the official, who asked not to be named. "The centre is open to the public once again after a temporary closure."
The hoax call came a day after the Islamic fundamentalist Jamaat-i-Islami party held an anti-American demonstration in Islamabad and burned an effigy of President Bill Clinton.

The demonstrators were protesting remarks by a U.S. attorney in a television interview in June about the arrest and extradition of a Pakistani fugitive, Mir Aimal Kansi, the prime suspect in a deadly shooting outside CIA headquarters in 1993.
Pakistan said on Thursday that a controversy over the remarks attributed to attorney Robert Horan must now end, apparently backing down on its demand for a public apology.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that enough had been said about Horan's remarks, which sparked an outcry in Pakistan. "This matter can now be put to rest," he said.

Pakistani newspapers quoted Horan as saying in a June 23 television interview that people in the region where Kansi lived were backward and would hand over their mothers for much less than the $2 million U.S. reward offered in the hunt for Kansi.

Kansi, from the mainly tribal southwestern province of Baluchistan, bordering Afghanistan and Iran, was captured in June by U.S. FBI agents with the help of Pakistani commandos in an operation that sparked protests in Pakistan.
